tldr: Biggest surprise this run: the Fed Chair is Kevin Warsh, not Jerome Powell -- Warsh was Senate-confirmed 54-45 in May 2026 and ran Wednesday's FOMC press conference; every prior 'Powell' reference in this dashboard was stale.

FOMC held at 3.75-4.00% but on a 10-2 vote, with two governors (Cook, Hammack) dissenting IN FAVOR OF A HIKE -- an unusual hawkish dissent that pushed December-hike odds to ~82-86%, and a reported (news, not price-spine-verified) same-day reversal of the 10-year yield back above 5%.

Mega-cap earnings split sharply: Microsoft beat decisively (Azure +48%, EPS beat) and rose ~4-5% after-hours, while Alphabet missed on EPS/free cash flow -- partly an $8.2B unrealized markdown on its SpaceX stake -- and fell ~10-11% after-hours despite Google Cloud revenue nearly tripling.

Levered silver sleeve risk: gold and silver both eased into the hawkish FOMC decision and the gold-silver ratio widened to 75.1 (from ~60 in January) -- the real-yield relief that drove Tuesday's miner rally is now in question.

Regional flows are diverging hard: Korea's foreign/institutional buying extended to a second straight day (the largest foreign net buy in 51 days) even as Hong Kong Southbound hit an 11th straight net-sell day and China's margin balance fell to a year-to-date low.

Rare-earth truce risk is reduced but not resolved: China's Commerce Ministry confirmed the broader US-China trade truce extends to Jan 10, 2027, but never explicitly named rare-earth export controls, so the Nov 10, 2026 deadline remains a live, if lower-probability, risk for the MP/Lynas/Energy Fuels watchlist.
